input.title: Prod Repo pool is 3: POOL_SIZE comes from a terraform default, and the app env file's POOL_SIZE=10 is dead config
input.body: Read on prod (read-only): the Repo pool_size is 3, and queue_target and queue_interval are unset. Runtime config reads POOL_SIZE (default 10), but prod gets it from a parameter whose terraform default is 3, and no tfvars overrides it. The env file says POOL_SIZE=10, and nothing reads it. The background workers alone can want about 35 checkouts. Fix: size the pool per repo against the database's max_connections, remove or wire the dead env value, and assert the effective pool size in a check. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Background fan-outs (route, enrichment and click workers, a sweeper, off-path dispatch) are not budgeted against the Repo pool
input.body: Three workers each run 4 concurrent tasks on a 5 s tick, a sweeper runs 2, and off-path dispatch runs pool/2. With about 20 sequential periodic passes the worst case is 35-39 checkouts, before webhooks, MCP and LiveView, against a prod pool of 3. Fix: budget background concurrency against the configured pool size (derived, never hardcoded), so background work cannot starve request paths. Add a functional test of the budget. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Prod Repo runs DBConnection's default queue_target 50 ms / queue_interval 1 s, dropping checkouts in short bursts
input.body: The prod Repo uses DBConnection's defaults, queue_target 50 ms and queue_interval 1 s; config sets neither. They drop queued checkouts in short bursts: the errors during the incident read "dropped after 654-1950ms". Choose deliberate values together with the pool sizing ticket. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Eight repos share one small RDS instance: per-repo pool sizing and RDS headroom unchecked
input.body: Eight repos times POOL_SIZE share one db.t3.micro. Its CPU credits and connection count during the incident were not checked. Read the CloudWatch metrics, then size the per-repo pools and the RDS headroom. The app host's low load says nothing about the database. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Periodic worker ticks align from boot (no jitter), so worker cohorts hit the Repo pool together
input.body: Every periodic worker schedules its first tick with send_after(interval) from boot, with no jitter, so the 5 s and 15 s cohorts fire together. The workers that crashed during the incident are exactly those cohorts. Fix: a deterministic stagger on the first tick, tested with an injected value, not a clock. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Priorities rule update rescores row by row under FOR UPDATE and blocks ingests
input.body: The priorities rule update rescores row by row under FOR UPDATE, holding a connection and row locks for the whole rescore and blocking ingests meanwhile. Batch it or bound the transaction. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Ack-timeout, route-heads and unjudged queries scan the whole backlog every tick
input.body: Three per-tick backlog queries scan the whole backlog each tick (ack timeouts, route heads, and unjudged requests, which have no index on their revision column). Read EXPLAIN on prod-shaped data and add the indexes or bounds they need. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Summary store prune and delete_disabled are not batched
input.body: The summary store's prune and delete_disabled are not batched: each is one statement over every matching row. Batch them so a large prune cannot hold a connection and locks for long. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Prod API returns 500 on every request since today's release: a migration renamed a column the running code still reads
input.body: Since the 14:10Z release every request to the production API returns HTTP 500. The release's migration renamed accounts.email to accounts.login_email, but the running release still selects accounts.email, so every authenticated query raises. No user can sign in or load a page right now. Fix: ship a release that reads the new column, or roll the migration back. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Nightly prune deletes other owners' live summaries: its DELETE has no owner filter
input.body: The nightly prune job's DELETE has no owner_id filter, so it removes every summary older than 30 days for every owner, not only the disabled ones it targets. Last night it deleted 1,240 live rows, and there is no backup of that table. It runs again at 02:00 tonight and will delete more. Fix: add the owner and disabled filters, and stop the job until it ships. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Public export endpoint returns any owner's records for any id with no authorization check
input.body: GET /api/v1/export/:owner_id is routed outside the authenticated pipeline. Any unauthenticated caller on the internet can download any owner's full record set by changing the id, and the ids are sequential. It is live in production now.

input.title: Production app crash-loops on boot: runtime config raises on an env var today's release added
input.body: The production app has been crash-looping since 09:00Z: runtime config raises because the new FEATURE_KEY variable is not set in prod, so the release never boots and the site is down for every user. Fix: set the variable or make it optional, then redeploy.

input.title: Webhook events are lost for good: the outbox table is truncated on every deploy
input.body: The deploy script truncates the webhook outbox table on every deploy, so any event not yet delivered is deleted with no copy anywhere. Every deploy loses customer events permanently, and there are several deploys a day. Fix: remove the truncate and drain the outbox before a deploy. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: ticket-classify crashes on any body containing an emoji, so no agent can file a ticket
input.body: ticket-classify raises Encoding::CompatibilityError on any body file that holds a 4-byte UTF-8 character, and exits before printing the filer's values. Every agent's filing step runs it, so filing stops for the whole fleet whenever a body quotes an emoji. There is no flag to skip it. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Merge guard accepts a gate receipt for a different head SHA, so an ungated tree can land
input.body: The merge guard checks that an integration receipt exists for the branch, but not that its SHA is the head being merged. A push after the gate lands with the old receipt, so an ungated tree reaches main. Nothing else re-checks it.

input.title: Owner's group DMs are routed to the wrong session every time
input.body: Every group DM the owner sends is routed to the harness session, whatever its topic, because the router reads the channel kind before the topic. The owner has no way to send a group DM to the right session.

input.title: lead-time report counts a reverted PR as landed
input.body: lead-time counts a PR that was merged and then reverted as landed, so the weekly median is understated. Reading the PR list by hand gives the right number. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: inbox-status reports zero unread when the registry entry is missing
input.body: inbox-status prints 0 unread and exits 0 when the project's registry entry is missing, so a dark channel reads as a quiet one. inbox-doctor names the missing entry if run by hand.

input.title: Contract cites a flag that was renamed
input.body: The contract's eval section still names --labels-file, which was renamed to --labels. The tool's --help is right; only the prose is stale. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).

input.title: Unused helper format_age left behind after the refactor
input.body: format_age in the shared lib has no callers since the refactor. Delete it.

input.body: test-slot --help spells 'receive' as 'recieve' in the queue paragraph. Source: DND-9000 captain report (pool-starvation findings), ai-artifacts/coordination/2026-01-01-example/reports/DND-9000-report.md. Context: the 16:00Z 2026-01-01 prod outage (DND-9000).
